note: [agent-bulk] nuecc, 38 showers - the busiest event in my shard. Vertex judged from the native r95 framing (event_half_span_cm 107.1, below the 150 cm re-capture threshold): the blue star sits at a junction where the long track bends and a second prong leaves, with 6001 (pdg 2212, 68.0 cm) and 6064 (pdg 13, 10.1 cm) both reading dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 and BOTH correctly left grey. It is the least clean vertex I looked at - on vtx-az-055-el+60 there is charge on both sides of the star along one line - but two prongs nearly back-to-back in projection explain that, so I am NOT calling it vertex-bad. shw 6063 (115.1 MeV, 3 segments, pdg 11, len 32.7, start ON the vertex): the member set is essentially one 31.0 cm body plus two sub-cm bits (34021 at 58.2 cm / 8.1 deg, 40027 at 20.7 cm / 24.1 deg). It does have real transverse spread on az+085 - the charge cloud is visibly wider than the polyline - so unlike evt173819 and evt179611 in this shard I am NOT questioning that it is EM. THE FINDING, and why the radio says under-clustered: on the acceptance plot 6004 (3.0 cm) sits at 8.7 cm / 19.1 deg, i.e. STRICTLY INSIDE the pass-1 box (25 deg out to 80 cm), closer AND at a smaller angle than the accepted member 40027 which sits at 24.1 deg right on the 25 deg line - yet 6004 was not taken. A non-member inside the box while a member sits at the edge of it is the cleanest single acceptance-plot signal I saw in ten events. WHY THE CONFIDENCE IS unclear. (1) MAGNITUDE: 6004 is 3.0 cm and below the 20 MeV scope threshold, against a 115.1 MeV / 32.7 cm shower, so even if I am right the effect is small and calling the event under-clustered arguably overstates it. (2) CORRECTION 11: 6004 is NOT grey - it is the seed of its own sub-20 MeV shower, so this rests on the 'owned by a neighbour' basis the corrections warn is unsafe. RECONCILIATION RUN, and it PASSES: the shower dict reports nseg = 3, the owner-grouped candidate rows for 6063 are exactly three (6063, 34021, 40027), and the shower's own cmp_div reads 'already in shower 6063 : 3 segment(s) plotted -- distance 0.0-58.2 cm, angle 0.0-24.1 deg'. Three ways of counting agree, so 6004 is NOT a hidden second-owner member of 6063 the way the evt280972 segments were - it is genuinely outside the member set, and the finding is not the correction-11 trap. I marked 6004 IN and it is the WEAK mark on this event - it is the one I would let the owner reverse. Nothing GREY is missing: apart from the two vertex hadrons at dist 0 and 6008 (pdg 2212, 3.3 cm) at 79.9 deg, every unowned segment is at 47-81 deg, well outside the cone. Second object: shw 23019 (99.6 MeV in a SINGLE 18.9 cm segment) sits 12.6 cm away at 70.8 deg - a separate prong, not part of 6063's cone, and 99.6 MeV in one 19 cm segment is a track/PID question I am not resolving. pi0: showers[].pio_id is -1 for all three in-scope showers, no group accepted; the capture auto-slots 6063 + 23019 for a placeholder m = 166.2 MeV at theta 101.8 deg, but both are vertex-attached so neither can be a conversion and I store no candidate. NOT LOOKED AT: 35 of the 38 showers - everything the scope rule skipped below 20 MeV min_kine_best - and of the 3 in scope I opened frames for 6063 only, reading 23019 and 51038 (66.7 MeV, pdg 13) off the candidate table. This verdict is a claim about 6063, not about the event.
